questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to start a clothing business
The health problems that many women face during pregnancy
A project that sews pads for women who need them
Why refugees are moving to the UK
questions.why: They learn about a project fighting period poverty that affects thousands of women refugees.

options: Being too ill to work during your period
Not being able to get or afford period products
Earning less money than men
Not being taught anything about periods at school
questions.why: Georgie says it's when people don't have access to these products or can't afford them.

questions.q: Which effect of period poverty does Georgie mention?
options: Women move to other countries
Families have to spend less money on food each week
Shops raise their prices
Girls miss school, which affects their education
questions.why: She says girls on their periods not going to school affects their education.

questions.q: How did Ella Lambert learn to make pads?
options: She taught herself with a borrowed sewing machine and YouTube
She took a sewing course at Bristol University during lockdown
Her grandmother showed her
She worked in a clothes factory
questions.why: She borrowed a sewing machine from a friend and learned how to sew on YouTube.

questions.q: Why does Ella say she still can't sew anything except pads?
options: To show she learned to sew only for this project
To complain that sewing is much too difficult to learn
To explain why the project stopped
To ask listeners to teach her
questions.why: She was so focused on pads that, “to this day”, they're the only thing she can sew.

questions.q: How are Ella's pads different from most pads sold in shops?
options: They are much thinner
They are made of paper
They can be washed and used again
They are only made for young girls at school
questions.why: Beth says Ella designed them to be washed and used again, unlike disposable shop pads.

questions.q: Who has the Pachamama Project given period products to?
options: Only students and staff at Bristol University during lockdown
Refugees from Syria, Turkey and Lebanon, and women in the UK
Hospitals across Europe
Schools in South America
questions.why: Georgie says they donated to refugees in Syria, Turkey and Lebanon, as well as women in the UK.

questions.q: What change has Ella noticed among the women giving out the pads?
options: They have stopped using the pads
They now keep the pads hidden behind a curtain
They only talk about periods with other women, never with men
They now talk about periods openly, even with men
questions.why: At first they barely spoke about it; now they chat away about the pads with male colleagues.
